claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode, SUPERSEDED, locks a stage to one execution at a time.
CodePipeline's SUPERSEDED execution mode only protects an execution once it is actually running, not while it is waiting to enter a locked stage.
Under CodePipeline's SUPERSEDED execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.

If a CodeBuild pipeline stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress.
Setting a CodePipeline's execution mode to QUEUED causes waiting executions to form a queue so each one runs in turn rather than a later commit erasing an earlier one that never got its turn.
The QUEUED execution mode requires a V2 pipeline in AWS CodePipeline.
Setting a CodePipeline to QUEUED execution mode requires setting both the `executionMode` and `pipelineType` fields when defining the pipeline.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can be used to set the pipeline's `executionMode` and `pipelineType`.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` Pulumi resource exposes `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs that can be set to configure a CodePipeline as code.
Using Pulumi ESC to broker short-lived cloud credentials avoids storing provider keys as pipeline variables at all.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the deployment lease to only one of them.
When Pulumi Cloud grants the deployment lease to only one of two simultaneous runs targeting the same stack, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines can prevent concurrent-run stack conflicts at the source with an exclusive lock check on the environment a deployment job targets.
An Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check is added from an environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior` is a setting configured on the stage that references an environment's exclusive lock check.

An Azure Pipelines `Pulumi@1` task with `command: up`, `stack: acme/website/production`, and `args: --yes` can be used within a `runOnce` deployment strategy on a stage with `lockBehavior: sequential`.
claims.source_hint: Azure DevOps / Pulumi Azure Pipelines task (Pulumi@1)

claims.text: `runLatest` is the default `lockBehavior` value for an Azure Pipelines stage referencing an exclusive lock check.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run ever acquires the lock, so an older run stuck waiting behind it is passed over rather than eventually applied.
Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: runLatest` behavior is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage runs against the lock in order, one at a time.
Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: sequential` serializes queued stage runs the same way Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack.
The Azure DevOps provider's `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource can be used to manage an Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check as code.
Azure DevOps itself — including projects, repositories, pipelines, and service connections — can be managed as code with the Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry.
Pulumi offers native version control integrations for popular Git hosts, independent of TeamCity.
When a Pulumi version control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud posts infrastructure-change summaries as pull request comments and status checks.
When a Pulumi version control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud links each stack update back to the commit and pull request that produced it.
If two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When Pulumi Cloud grants the stack update lease to only one of two concurrent runs, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's own default behavior is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as it has available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option called 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under that configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option defaults to 0, meaning unlimited concurrent builds.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first build instead.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to 1 causes a queued second build to run only once the first build finishes.

Limiting TeamCity's simultaneous builds to 1 produces the same one-at-a-time behavior that Pulumi Cloud's own per-stack lease gives, applied earlier in the process so the build never gets far enough to hit an update conflict.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment a deployment job targets, with `lockBehavior: sequential` set on the stage, serializes deployments so they do not overlap.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check that can be added to the environment a deployment job targets.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock exists and documents serializing deployments with an exclusive lock.
AWS CodePipeline has a pipeline-level setting called 'execution mode' that can be set to `QUEUED`.
Setting an AWS CodePipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` causes waiting executions to run in turn (serialized) instead of the default behavior.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode lets a newer pipeline execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/#serialize-pipeline-executions exists and documents serializing pipeline executions.
TeamCity has a build-configuration-level setting called 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' that can be set to `1` to prevent concurrent deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/#limit-concurrent-builds exists and documents limiting concurrent builds in TeamCity.
